doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Les Paul's temperament and the Monday night tribute gig
summary: Les was always kind to her, missed her when she toured, and she sends Jay Leonhart as sub at the Monday Tribute to Les Paul night.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I guess you can learn from all those things, but it seems like he didn’t suffer fools gladly.

Les? No. No. No. He was always good to me. Always good to me. You know sometimes he’d get mad because I went on the road. I couldn’t be there every Monday night for ten years, you know what I mean? I was really trying to, I love going to Europe and playing. I love going to certain places and I just couldn’t turn that down to stay in New York for Monday night and maybe some other gigs during the week that might turn up. It was hard to make a living just on that Monday night. So you know sometimes — but he usually said, “We missed you.” And sometimes that’s all he’d say the whole night. But if we had a really great show he’d say, “That was fun” or something, “that was good.” And if it wasn’t such a good show or he wasn’t happy with his playing he wouldn’t say really anything. But it was never really negative, ever, towards me or the musicians. And he enjoyed it. And he had a good time. And he laughed all the time. And he was funny.
And now that gig — you have a series of different people who come in?
Yeah. It’s the Tribute to Les Paul Night every Monday, so same as before I’m there most Monday nights, but sometimes I’m not if I’m on the road.
Is it your job to send in a sub?
Absolutely. Jay Leonhart subs for me.
Oh. How funny is that. That’s funny.
Yeah. Well I wanted someone that could also sing a tune, and Jay has a wonderful repertoire, and you know, comedic songs and playing the bass essentially.
